## Tested scope

The Python inspector validates v2 core envelope structure with a 16 KiB encoded/JSON bound, at most 32 alternatives, and bounded integer amounts. HTTP uses the canonical challenge header; MCP checks agreement of structured and text error payloads. Unknown schemes can have valid envelopes without being executable. Legacy v1 and future versions are reported as unsupported. These are diagnostic resource limits, not universal protocol limits.

The local spending helper supports exact EVM authorization-flow alternatives under an explicit single-operation policy. It does not implement aggregate budget reservations or wallet signing. The SDK fixture exercises real HTTP negotiation, locally generated EVM signatures, and independent signature/tamper verification with an in-memory mock facilitator; facilitator verification/settlement replies are synthetic. It performs no RPC or funded transaction. Settlement success, rejection, and uncertain transport outcome are separate states. The local operation guard prevents repeat/concurrent settlement attempts for the same operation and rejects a changed payment under that operation ID. Its in-memory state is an example, not durable crash recovery or facilitator-wide idempotency.

MPP detection checks authentication syntax, required envelope fields, and a decoded request object. It does not validate method-specific request semantics, JCS canonicalization, challenge binding, or settlement. A recognized surface is not full MPP conformance. Unrelated 402 bodies do not count.

## Maintenance

Update pins and failure vectors together. Run `x402-agentic-payments/scripts/test_conformance.py`, `commerce-readiness/scripts/test_payments.py`, and the SDK fixture. After editing `scripts/payment_challenges.py`, run repository `scripts/sync_payment_parser.py`; `scripts/validate_inventory.py` checks the self-contained readiness copy stays identical. Do not import another installed plugin's filesystem resources.

Fixtures are original synthetic inputs informed by the cited specifications, not copied vendor test vectors. Compare future SDK/schema changes explicitly before broadening support.
